title: LandscapeLockfile

resolution.description: One entry per requested term. Every entry is fully pinned: an artifact_id alone is not enough because channels move.

artifact_id.description:
The artifact coordinate, or - for a term computed by shipped code rather than by a model - a builtin coordinate `builtin:<term_id>:<engine_version>`.

The builtin form was added during P1-28. The rung vocabulary below has always admitted `builtin`, but this field required an ArtifactId, whose grammar begins `cf:<kind>:` and has no spelling for a term that has no artifact. So a lockfile recording a CAI resolution could not be written. The alternative fixes were both worse: allowing null loses the engine version, which is the only thing identifying what computed the number, and stretching ArtifactId itself would let a builtin coordinate appear in `model_pins`, where it means nothing.

digest.description: For an artifact, its content digest. For a builtin, the digest of the engine descriptor `{engine, term_id, version}` - a real hash of a real document, so that changing the engine version changes the lockfile, rather than a sentinel that merely looks like a digest.

host_distance.description: Populated only when resolved_by = nearest_host. Records why this substitution was considered acceptable and by how much uncertainty was inflated.

engines.description: Non-model compute engines whose version changes the numbers (structure folding above all).

structure_parameters_digest.description: Digest of the structure_parameters document in force, or null when no structure term ran. DEP-STRU-001: thermodynamic parameters are user-supplied input data rather than a compiled-in table, so two runs are only comparable if they agree here. A different parameter set is a different energy model, and every fold it produced is a different answer.

rng.description: Determinism contract. A parallel search is only reproducible if each worker's stream is derived deterministically from the root seed and the reduction order is fixed - floating-point summation is not associative, so 'same seed, different thread count' is otherwise a different answer.

stream_assignment.description:
per_block_index and per_individual_index are thread-count-independent; per_worker is not and is only legal for `fast` tier.

A run that derives streams at several granularities - per generation for the population loop, per block for tier 2 - records the FINEST one it uses, because that is the one that determines whether the run is thread-count independent. Recording a coarser granularity would understate the guarantee; recording per_worker when any finer scheme is in use would overstate the risk.

deterministic_reduction.description: When true, all cross-thread float reductions use a fixed tree order. Costs ~3% throughput and is required for any published result.

digest.description: The digest omits `created_at` as well as itself (`DEP-VER-003`): a document's identity is what it says, not when it was written, and a time-dependent digest makes `replay --assert-identical` impossible.
